headline: No documented interaction pathway; both open-source lists are non-runnable and network-egress-free, so pairwise risks are limited to hypothetical manual misuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither agent is runnable, and both profiles show no I/O surfaces or shared channel. With no filesystem, clipboard, MCP, or network bridge documented, there is no plausible default prompt-injection pathway between awesome-nlp and awesome-production-machine-learning.
conditions: IF either profile gains a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge, reassess injection risk.
IF either agent becomes runnable and parses the other's output as instructions, risk increases.
mitigations: Keep both agents non-runnable in the current deployment.
Do not add shared clipboard or workspace mounts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared channel is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents report network_egress:none and touch no data classes, so there is no documented path for sensitive data to flow from one to the other or out to a third party. The pairwise leakage pathway is therefore not evidenced in either profile.
conditions: IF either agent begins handling sensitive data classes, re-evaluate leakage.
IF either agent is given outbound network access, leakage risk changes.
mitigations: Keep outbound network disabled for both agents.
Avoid placing secrets in any shared workspace.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls before enabling data-bearing workflows.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write-capable surfaces are documented: both profiles lack filesystem, database, git, or OAuth permissions, and both are non-runnable. Without shared mutable resources, there is no capability conflict between the pair.
conditions: IF either agent is granted write access to the same mutable resource, reassess conflict.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locks or shared state, conflict analysis changes.
mitigations: Do not co-locate them on a shared writable workspace.
requires-engineering: introduce locking if shared mutable state is later added.

D_cascading_error.rationale: These are curated awesome-lists, not action-taking agents, so one does not appear to automatically consume the other's outputs. Any cascade would require manual copying or an external orchestrator, making the pathway unusual and the blast radius small.
conditions: IF an external workflow starts treating one list as authoritative input to the other, cascade risk increases.
IF either agent is wrapped in an automation that executes downstream actions, reassess.
mitigations: Require human review before reusing one agent's output.
Do not auto-feed outputs between the two agents.
requires-engineering: add verification gates if downstream automation is introduced.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented, and both profiles touch no data classes. Because the compliance dimensions in the rubric are absent here, there is no evidenced compliance breach to assign.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data, reassess compliance.
IF residency or retention policies are added, compare them explicitly.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair.
Document residency and retention before any data-bearing use.
requires-engineering: add policy checks if compliance-scoped data is introduced.
